10.01.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "chondrosarcoma"
- "AP (anteroposterior) X-ray of the proximal femur, physis **closed**: a **metaphyseal, central, mixed** lesion with **ill-defined** margins."
- "The cortex shows **thickening and deep endosteal scalloping**. Rings-and-arcs calcification. So → **malignant**."
- "In a patient over 40 my differential is **chondrosarcoma**, enchondroma (if painless, short, no scalloping), bone infarct, metastasis."
- "Next → CT (computed tomography) for the scalloping, MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) of the whole bone, chest CT, bone scan, then **biopsy** by the treating team. Treatment → **wide resection**; grade 1 in a limb → extended curettage."

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **>40, male · pelvis, proximal femur, central · rings and arcs + deep scalloping · malignant chondrocytes, no osteoid · wide resection**

### 1 Definition
- Chondrosarcoma → **malignant** · cartilage origin; **any malignant osteoid → chondroblastic osteosarcoma** (Campbell)
- Grade 1 in a limb → **atypical cartilaginous tumour** (ACT, low-grade cartilage neoplasm): metastasis <1% (OKU Tumors 4)

### 2 Origin
- **Primary** → de novo in the medulla · **secondary** → on a benign cartilage lesion · gene → **IDH1/IDH2** mutations in ≈50% (OKU Tumors 4)

| Precursor | Risk |
|---|---|
| Solitary osteochondroma | ≈1% (Campbell) |
| **Multiple hereditary exostoses** | ≈5–10% lifetime (Campbell) |
| Solitary enchondroma | Low; no prophylactic surgery |
| **Ollier disease** · **Maffucci** | ≈25% by age 40 · higher (Campbell) |
| Others | Synovial chondromatosis, chondroblastoma, radiation, fibrous dysplasia |

### 3 Incidence
- **Age** → **40–60** primary · 25–45 secondary (Campbell) · **Sex** → male, up to 2 : 1 · general rule
- **Relative incidence** → Rank → **2nd commonest** non-haematologic primary bone malignancy (Campbell)

### 4 Sites
- **Longitudinal** → **metaphyseal + diaphyseal** of proximal long bones; clear cell → **epiphyseal** · **Transverse** → **central**; periosteal type → surface
- **Special** → **pelvis** commonest, proximal femur, humerus, ribs (Miller) · hand → rare, yet the **commonest primary bone malignancy of the hand** (Campbell)

- Sites, age and sex of chondrosarcoma, diagram (Greenspan)

### 5 Clinical presentation
| Local | Systemic | Complications by location |
|---|---|---|
| **Pain** slowly increasing, mass · high grade → weeks | None in low grade | Pelvis → huge mass · spine → neurological · fracture rare |

CLINICAL PEARL — pain in a cartilage lesion
- Pain **without a fracture** in a cartilage lesion → think low-grade chondrosarcoma, not enchondroma (Campbell)

| Behavior · Margins | **Mixed**: lysis + chondroid calcification · wide zone of transition in higher grades |
| Cortical reaction | **Thickening + deep endosteal scalloping**; breach + mass in grade 2–3 |
| Special signs | **Rings and arcs** (annular, comma-shaped), popcorn calcification (Greenspan) |

- Proximal femur, 66-year-old woman | distal femur, 46-year-old man (Greenspan)

### 7 Labs
- **Routine** → **Basic labs only**

### 8 Biopsy
- **Modality** → Needle biopsy **under-grades** (heterogeneous tissue) → grade by film + site + histology · expendable site → resection without biopsy · **Open biopsy rules** → contamination → high recurrence
- Gross → blue-grey lobules · microscopy → hypercellular, **binucleate** cells, **entrapment of host trabeculae** · exclusion → malignant osteoid

- Chondrosarcoma histology, entrapped trabeculae (Campbell)

CLINICAL PEARL — the needle lies
- Core needle often gets only bland hyaline cartilage → grade the lesion by its **film and site** (OKU Tumors 4)

### 9 Differential diagnosis
- **Location groups** → **By location** → central cartilage lesion in an adult long bone: **malignant until proved otherwise** · **by cortex** → enchondroma (no scalloping, painless) → 6 Cartilage
- **Histology groups** → **By cell** → no giant cells; mesenchymal type has round cells · **Special DD** → **the mimic** → bone infarct; GCT at the articular end; chordoma in the sacrum → 12 Chordoma

HIGH YIELD — malignant + calcification
- Real question (Nagah p19): adult, **malignant-looking lesion with rings-and-arcs calcification** → **chondrosarcoma** · cloud-like tumour bone → osteosarcoma → 9 Osteosarcoma (Greenspan)

### 10 Grading
- **Enneking** + **AJCC** (American Joint Committee on Cancer) → 2 Work-up · histological grade → cellularity, atypia, binucleation, myxoid change

- Histology of grade 1/ACT, grade 2 and grade 3 (Gazendam 2023, open access)

| Grade | Histology | Film | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 / ACT** (≈60%) | Few binucleate cells | Scalloping, cortex intact, no mass | Metastasis <1% in limbs (OKU Tumors 4) |
| **2** | Moderate atypia, myxoid | Cortex breached, mass | Metastasis 5–15% |
| **3** | Marked atypia, mitoses, necrosis | Destruction, large mass | Metastasis >30% |

- **Malignant local** → **Surgical disease**: chemo- and radio-resistant · grade 1, limb, in the medulla → **extended curettage** + high-speed burr ± adjuvant (OKU Tumors 4)

- Grade 1 curettage → PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate) filler · grade 3 scapula → Tikhoff-Linberg resection

10.02.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "Ewing sarcoma"
- "AP X-ray of the femur, physis **open**: a **diaphyseal, central, osteolytic** lesion with **ill-defined (permeative)** margins."
- "The cortex shows **destruction** with **onion-skin** periosteal reaction and a large soft-tissue mass. So → **malignant**."
- "In a child my differential is **Ewing sarcoma**, osteomyelitis, eosinophilic granuloma; lymphoma if older."
- "Next → MRI of the whole bone, chest CT, bone scan or PET (positron emission tomography), then **biopsy with culture**. Treatment → chemotherapy, local control (surgery or radiotherapy), chemotherapy."

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **5–25, male · diaphysis + pelvis · permeative, onion skin, big mass · small round blue cells, CD99 · chemo + surgery/RT**

### 1 Definition
- Ewing sarcoma → **malignant** · unknown origin → **small round blue cell** sarcoma; PNET (primitive neuroectodermal tumour) same family · always **high grade**

### 2 Origin
- Marrow or neural crest · gene → **t(11;22)(q24;q12) EWS-FLI1** ≈85–90% (Greenspan) · Ewing-like sarcomas without EWSR1 → Ewing protocols

### 3 Incidence
- **Age** → **5–25**; 90% before 25 (Greenspan) · **Sex** → male · rare in people of African descent
- **Relative incidence** → Rank → **2nd commonest** bone malignancy in the young; commonest under 10 (Campbell)

PITFALL — age range
- Handbook → 5–30 · Greenspan, Campbell → 5–25
- Say → "**5 to 25**; under 5 think neuroblastoma or leukaemia, over 30 think metastasis"

### 4 Sites
- **Longitudinal** → **diaphyseal** or metadiaphyseal · **Transverse** → **central**, whole marrow · hands and feet rare
- Order → lower limb 41% · **pelvis 26%** · chest wall 16% (OKU Tumors 4) · **special** → pelvis, ribs, scapula

- Sites, age and sex of Ewing sarcoma, diagram (Greenspan)

### 5 Clinical presentation
| Local | Systemic | Complications by location |
|---|---|---|
| **Pain**, enlarging mass, warmth; diagnosis delayed months | **Fever**, weight loss · high ESR (erythrocyte sedimentation rate), CRP (C-reactive protein), white cells | Spine → bowel, bladder · pelvis → longest delay |

- Fever + local signs + high ESR → **mistaken for osteomyelitis** · metastasis at presentation ≈25% → **lung**, then bone (OKU Tumors 4)

| Margins | **Permeative or moth-eaten** |
| Cortical reaction | **Onion skin** or sunburst; **saucerization**; **large soft-tissue mass** |
| Special signs | Mass large compared with the bone destruction (Greenspan) |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### 7 Labs

### 8 Biopsy
- **Modality** → Core needle with FISH or PCR for the translocation, at a sarcoma centre · aspirate may look like **pus** → culture **and** pathology (Prof Abosena)
- Child <5 with fever and pain, equivocal films → biopsy; no core service → small exploration biopsy down to bone (Prof Abosena)

CLINICAL PEARL — culture what you biopsy
- **Culture what you biopsy, biopsy what you culture**; tissue not reassuring → no debridement until pathology returns (Prof Abosena)

- Gross → soft grey-white, "brain-like" · microscopy → sheets of **small round blue cells**, **PAS +** glycogen
- **CD99 (MIC2)** + FLI1; CD45 negative (lymphoma positive) (OKU Tumors 4) · Homer-Wright rosettes → PNET end

- Ewing histology, small round blue cells (OKU Tumors 4)

### 9 Differential diagnosis
- **Location groups** → **By location** → diaphyseal lesion in a child: Ewing, osteomyelitis, eosinophilic granuloma · **by cortex** → non-expansile, permeative, onion skin, mass
- **Histology groups** → **By cell** → round cells by age: <5 neuroblastoma, leukaemia · 5–25 Ewing · >30 lymphoma, myeloma, metastasis · **Special DD** → **the mimic** → **osteomyelitis**, real question no. 3 (Nagah p31)

| Feature (Greenspan) | Ewing sarcoma | Osteomyelitis | Eosinophilic granuloma | Lymphoma |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Duration for the same destruction | **4–6 months** | **4–6 weeks** | **7–10 days** | — |
| Soft tissue | **Well-defined mass**, fat planes kept | Diffuse swelling, **planes lost** | Little or no mass | Little mass |
| Periosteal reaction | Onion skin, sunburst | Lamellated, involucrum | Lamellated possible | Usually little |
| Other | Saucerization | Sequestrum | Bevelled edges, hole-in-hole | Older, CD45+  |

- MRI → central breakdown + **rim enhancement** = infection; whole marrow, no rim = Ewing · PET-CT and bone scan both light up → only biopsy decides (Prof Abosena)

CLINICAL PEARL — the clock and the planes
- Same destruction in **weeks** → infection; in **months** → Ewing; a **sharp mass with fat planes kept** → Ewing (Greenspan)

- Film beside film: Ewing | osteomyelitis | eosinophilic granuloma | lymphoma (Greenspan)

| Film | Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ewing | metaphyseal + diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | ill-defined (permeative) | lamellated periosteal reaction + soft-tissue mass | fever, 8 weeks | **malignant** |
| Osteomyelitis | metaphyseal + diaphyseal | central | mixed | ill-defined | destruction + periosteal new bone | short history | **benign aggressive** |
| Eosinophilic granuloma | diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | ill-defined (permeative) | onion-skin periosteal reaction | 10 days of symptoms | **benign aggressive** |
| Lymphoma | metaphyseal + diaphyseal | central | osteolytic | ill-defined (permeative) | lamellated periosteal reaction | older patient | **malignant** |

### 10 Grading
- Always **high grade**; usually **AJCC** IIA or IIB at presentation → 2 Work-up

### 11 Treatment
- **Systemic** → **Neoadjuvant chemotherapy → local control → adjuvant chemotherapy** · **VDC/IE**: vincristine, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide alternating with ifosfamide, etoposide (OKU Tumors 4)
- **Malignant local** → **Surgery** if a wide margin and good function → local control 94% vs 80%, EFS (event-free survival) 66% vs 48% versus radiotherapy alone (OKU Tumors 4)
- **Radiotherapy** → radiosensitive; unresectable or morbid sites, after marginal resection · after chemotherapy → **ossifies**, mass shrinks → restage (Campbell)

- Clavicle, before and after 4 months of chemotherapy, then en bloc, 11-year-old boy (Greenspan)

| Site | Centralization | Behavior | Margins | Cortical reaction | Special signs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| clavicle | — | osteolytic | ill-defined | destruction + soft-tissue mass | sclerotic after chemotherapy | **malignant** |

- Pathological fracture → splint, chemotherapy, then decide; survival not significantly changed (OKU Tumors 4) · reconstruction → 3 Treatment principles

PITFALL — "chemotherapy + radiotherapy"
- Handbook → chemotherapy + radiotherapy · OKU, Campbell → **surgery when a wide margin is possible**
- Say → "**chemotherapy, then surgery if resectable, radiotherapy if not**"

### 12 Prognosis & complications
- **Prognosis** → Long-term survival → <10% before chemotherapy · **60–75%** localized now · 20–30% metastatic (Campbell)
- Worse → **metastasis** (strongest) · axial > proximal > **distal limb** · large size · LDH, fever · <90% necrosis (OKU Tumors 4) · **Tumour-specific** → late effects → second cancers, growth

- **Translocation and marker?** → t(11;22) EWS-FLI1; CD99
- **Local control?** → surgery if resectable with good function; radiotherapy if not
- **Worst prognostic factor?** → metastasis at diagnosis
